newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up but demand still lacking.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up but demand still lacking.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week higher but demand was still absent with no immediate sign of improvement, said dealers.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 310 cents ($1.24) a kg, up one cent from Thursday. November SMR 20 buyer was half cent higher at 306.50.

Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 305-306 cents, SMR 10 at 306-307, SMR 5 at 311-312, SMR L at 343, SMR CV at 361-362 and drum latex at 233-234 cents. "It's been a very tight market and I don't expect it to improve by next week," said a dealer.
Traders, analysing market trends since Monday, said buyers appeared comfortably stocked after an active round of short-covering in the last two months.

"Usually, demand begins to slow down after every October but this year, it's a bit unusual as buyers began covering much earlier," said a dealer. Another trader said rains have reduced tapping and supply of latex but prices remained unaffected.
The INRO five-day average fell to 238.77 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 17 from 238.92 on Oct 16. The daily indicator also fell to 238.77 from 238.86 previously.
